findings.summary: Bot allow-list hardcodes `yorkie-agent[bot]`, but the App identity is a maintainer-provided secret — if the installed App's slug differs, the allow-list never matches and the fix/iterate steps stay blocked
findings.evidence: Both new lines set `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-review-panel.yml:413, agent-iterate-ci.yml:160). The bot login is derived at runtime from `secrets.AGENT_APP_ID` / `AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (agent-review-panel.yml:373-374), and docs/tasks/active/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md:75-77 explicitly says the App may be "the Claude GitHub App **or a dedicated app**". Nothing in the repo pins the slug to `yorkie-agent` (grep for `yorkie-agent` finds only these two new lines). If the configured App's slug is anything else, `allowed_bots` still excludes the actual initiating actor, claude-code-action keeps refusing the run, and the whole point of the change is defeated — now surfacing as a stalled page every cycle instead of a fix. A value derived from the minted token (e.g. the app-token step's `app-slug` output) would be correct.

findings.summary: `allowed_bots` may not be a supported input on the pinned claude-code-action commit, in which case it is silently ignored (warning only) and the bot block persists
findings.evidence: The action is pinned to the immutable commit `af0559ee4f514d1ef21826982bed13f7edc3c35e # v1` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:151, agent-review-panel.yml:404). GitHub Actions does not fail on an unknown `with:` key — it emits an "Unexpected input(s)" warning and continues. If `allowed_bots` was added to claude-code-action after that pinned commit, this change is a no-op: the human-actor check still throws, the fix step still fails, and the only observable difference is the new `stalled` page. I could not verify the pinned commit's action.yml inputs from this repo (the action is not vendored).

findings.summary: `stalled` now fires for promote/fix failures but still posts a message that claims the review panel produced no verdicts
findings.evidence: The `if` was widened to `needs.promote.result == 'failure' || needs.fix.result == 'failure'` (lines 459-460), yet the comment body is unconditional: "The review-panel job failed to complete. **A human should review** this PR — the automated panel did not produce verdicts." (line 479). When the panel succeeded and only the fixer agent errored, the paged human is told something factually wrong about where the pipeline broke, sending them to the wrong job.

findings.summary: A fix job that fails *after* claude-code-action pushed a commit posts the paged sentinel and permanently latches the fix loop off, even though a fresh CI/panel cycle is already in flight
findings.evidence: `needs.fix.result == 'failure'` (line 460) covers any failure of the 45-minute fix job, including a post-push failure or timeout after the agent already pushed the fix commit. `stalled` then unconditionally posts `<!-- agent-review-paged -->` (line 479). The fix guard treats that sentinel as a permanent latch — `if (comments.some((c) => c.body.includes(PAGED))) { proceed = 'false'; return; }` (line 324) — so the next (already-triggered) review round will never run a fix again, even if the pushed commit was fine. `stalled` does not check for an existing/inbound paged state or whether HEAD advanced before paging.

findings.summary: agent-iterate-ci gained the same `allowed_bots` fix but has no stalled/page safety net for a failing Claude step, so a refused or crashed fixer there still silently stalls
findings.evidence: The review-panel workflow adds a `stalled` job covering `fix.result == 'failure'` precisely because "a failed fix silently stalls a blocked PR" (agent-review-panel.yml:442-444). agent-iterate-ci.yml has exactly one job (`iterate`, line 33) with no equivalent safety net: if the "Run Claude Code" step (line 147) fails — the same bot-refusal or agent error the change is guarding against — no comment or `agent:needs-human-review` label is posted, no new commit is pushed, so no further CI run and no further `workflow_run` event occurs. The attempts guard (lines 68-112) only pages on MAX_ATTEMPTS *CI failures*, which will not increase, so the loop halts with no human notified.
searchedFor: read .github/workflows/agent-iterate-ci.yml in full (single `iterate` job, no `stalled`/`always()` job)

findings.summary: App token in the CI-fix job is minted with NO permission scoping, then handed to the LLM fixer this diff enables
findings.evidence: `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` at agent-iterate-ci.yml:93-96 is called with only `app-id`/`private-key` and NO `permission-*` inputs, so the minted token inherits the App installation's FULL permission set. That token is then (a) written into the workspace `.git/config` (checkout at lines 98-102, `persist-credentials` left at its default `true`), and (b) passed as `github_token:` to claude-code-action at line 322 — in a session where the agent has `Bash,Read,Edit,Write,Glob,Grep` (line 377) and runs untrusted branch code (`pnpm install`, `pnpm verify:fast`). The `allowed_bots` line added at 328 is what lets this step actually execute for the bot-initiated `workflow_run`, so the diff makes this exposure live rather than aborting at the actor check. The attacker vector is prompt injection through the branch-derived diagnosis interpolated at line 336 (see the separate finding on `failureSummary`): the agent can be steered to reuse the token for anything the App is granted beyond push/PR/issue — e.g. Workflows write (which would defeat the "the agent App cannot push .github/workflows/**" assumption stated at agent-review-panel.yml:51) or Administration. The same App token IS scoped everywhere else in the repo for exactly this reason: agent-review-panel.yml:1553-1555 (`permission-contents/pull-requests/issues`, commented "this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code"), agent-fix.yml:123-125, agent-review-on-demand.yml:484-488. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2037 concedes the App's "installation permissions the workflow block does not govern", so the job-level `permissions:` block at agent-iterate-ci.yml:24-30 does not bound this token. Confidence is medium only because the App's installed permission set is not readable from the repo; the missing scoping itself is certain.
searchedFor: docs/design/harness-engineering.md around 2020-2040 for App permission notes

findings.summary: Mutable `@v1` tag for the action that consumes AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, in the same job as the SHA-pinned claude-code-action step
findings.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:93 uses `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` — a movable tag — while receiving `secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (line 96). A retagged/compromised `v1` executes with the App private key in scope and can exfiltrate it, which is a strictly worse outcome than a leaked installation token (the key mints tokens for the whole installation, indefinitely). The repo's own standard is the opposite and is stated in-line: the neighbouring claude-code-action step in this same job is pinned to an immutable commit (line 319, "Pinned to the v1 release commit (immutable) for supply-chain safety"), and every other App-token site pins a SHA with the comment "this action handles the App private key" — agent-review-panel.yml:1282 and 1545, agent-fix.yml:116, agent-rerun.yml:89, agent-loop.yml:78, agent-summarize.yml:111/215, agent-review-on-demand.yml:107/480. Two other unpinned copies exist: agent-implement.yml:114 and agent-review-reply.yml:120. Out of diff, but in the job the diff re-activates.

findings.summary: `allowed_bots` includes the bare, squattable login `yorkie-agent` alongside the reserved `yorkie-agent[bot]`
findings.evidence: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:328 and agent-review-panel.yml:1640) adds a second entry without the `[bot]` suffix. The repo's own trust argument for bot logins depends on that suffix being unregisterable — agent-iterate-ci.yml:182-184 ("GitHub reserves the `[bot]` suffix for Apps") and agent-review-panel.yml:210-221 for PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS. `yorkie-agent` without the suffix is an ordinary account/org name in the public namespace, so if claude-code-action compares the raw actor login rather than normalising away a `[bot]` suffix, the bare entry allow-lists any actor whose login is exactly `yorkie-agent`, not just this App. It is not exploitable today: to be the actor of these `workflow_run` events an account must have caused a CI run on a base-repo branch, and the fork check at agent-iterate-ci.yml:44 / agent-review-panel.yml:155 rejects fork-PR actors — hence minor rather than higher. Either drop the bare entry (if the action normalises, it is redundant) or state in the comment which matching rule of the pinned action makes it safe.
searchedFor: read both claude-code-action steps in full
checked gate `if:` fork/enable clauses in both workflows
checked PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS reserved-suffix rationale in both files

findings.summary: Branch-controlled CI failure text is emitted verbatim inside a fixed `HARNESS_EOF` heredoc into GITHUB_OUTPUT and then into the fixer prompt
findings.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:287-292 captures `summarize-ci.mjs` stdout with a hard-coded delimiter (`echo "summary<<HARNESS_EOF"` … `echo "HARNESS_EOF"`). That stdout embeds `failureSummary` verbatim — scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs:97 does `out.push(`  ${failureSummary}`)`, and the two-space prefix applies only to the FIRST line, so any subsequent line of a multi-line build/test failure message is written unindented. A failure message whose body contains a line `HARNESS_EOF` therefore closes the heredoc early and the remaining bytes are parsed as further GITHUB_OUTPUT entries (arbitrary `key=value` for this step, or a malformed-file step failure). The same unsanitised text is interpolated into the fixer's prompt at line 336, so it can also forge the `</harness-diagnosis>` framing the surrounding "this is DATA, not instructions" guard relies on — against an agent holding Bash and the unscoped App token above. summarize-ci.mjs performs no delimiter filtering, escaping or truncation (whole file read; no `replace`/`slice` on the value). The archived adjudication that marked HARNESS_EOF a non-issue is explicitly scoped to the agent-implement kickoff prompt, whose content "is no longer agent-influenced" — docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md:172-174 — and does not cover this branch-derived path. Requires branch write access to reach, hence minor.

verdict.reason: Verified independently. Both cited lines exist verbatim: agent-iterate-ci.yml:160 and agent-review-panel.yml:413 hardcode `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"`, with adjacent comments stating the intent is to allow "ONLY our own App" so claude-code-action does not refuse the bot-initiated workflow_run. The App identity is however supplied entirely at runtime from maintainer secrets (agent-review-panel.yml:373-374, agent-iterate-ci.yml:59-60 use secrets.AGENT_APP_ID / AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY), and a repo-wide grep for `yorkie-agent` returns only those two lines — nothing pins, validates, or documents the installed App's slug. docs/tasks/active/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md:75-77 explicitly states the credentials may come from "the Claude GitHub App or a dedicated app", so the slug is maintainer-chosen; the repo itself is "Wafflebase" (README.md:1), making the literal even less self-evident. actions/create-github-app-token exposes an `app-slug` output that the workflows do not use, though they already consume steps.app-token.outputs.token. If the configured App's slug differs, the allow-list excludes the actual initiating actor, the fix/Run-Claude-Code steps are refused, and no fix is pushed. No guard prevents this: the `stalled` job (agent-review-panel.yml:448-459, comment at :443-444 explicitly anticipating "claude-code-action refusing a bot-initiated run") only pages a human, mitigating silence rather than the breakage. Considered refutation grounds: not-present fails (code is verbatim as described); already-guarded fails (the stalled page is a safety net, not a bypass-preventing guard); out-of-scope fails (a hardcoded constant that must match a runtime-derived identity, breaking the core autonomous fix loop when it does not, is a wrong-condition/broken-invariant defect in the correctness lane). I cannot rule out that the maintainer's App happens to be slugged yorkie-agent, but nothing in the repo establishes it, and that uncertainty keeps the finding.

The `allowed_bots` line added at 328 is what lets this step actually execute for the bot-initiated `workflow_run`, so the diff makes this exposure live rather than aborting at the actor check. The attacker vector is prompt injection through the branch-derived diagnosis interpolated at line 336 (see the separate finding on `failureSummary`): the agent can be steered to reuse the token for anything the App is granted beyond push/PR/issue — e.g. Workflows write (which would defeat the "the agent App cannot push .github/workflows/**" assumption stated at agent-review-panel.yml:51) or Administration. The same App token IS scoped everywhere else in the repo for exactly this reason: agent-review-panel.yml:1553-1555 (`permission-contents/pull-requests/issues`, commented "this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code"), agent-fix.yml:123-125, agent-review-on-demand.yml:484-488. docs/design/harness-engineering.md:2037 concedes the App's "installation permissions the workflow block does not govern", so the job-level `permissions:` block at agent-iterate-ci.yml:24-30 does not bound this token. Confidence is medium only because the App's installed permission set is not readable from the repo; the missing scoping itself is certain.
searchedFor: docs/design/harness-engineering.md around 2020-2040 for App permission notes

samples.summary: Mutable `@v1` tag for the action that consumes AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY, in the same job as the SHA-pinned claude-code-action step
samples.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:93 uses `actions/create-github-app-token@v1` — a movable tag — while receiving `secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY` (line 96). A retagged/compromised `v1` executes with the App private key in scope and can exfiltrate it, which is a strictly worse outcome than a leaked installation token (the key mints tokens for the whole installation, indefinitely). The repo's own standard is the opposite and is stated in-line: the neighbouring claude-code-action step in this same job is pinned to an immutable commit (line 319, "Pinned to the v1 release commit (immutable) for supply-chain safety"), and every other App-token site pins a SHA with the comment "this action handles the App private key" — agent-review-panel.yml:1282 and 1545, agent-fix.yml:116, agent-rerun.yml:89, agent-loop.yml:78, agent-summarize.yml:111/215, agent-review-on-demand.yml:107/480. Two other unpinned copies exist: agent-implement.yml:114 and agent-review-reply.yml:120. Out of diff, but in the job the diff re-activates.

samples.summary: `allowed_bots` includes the bare, squattable login `yorkie-agent` alongside the reserved `yorkie-agent[bot]`
samples.evidence: `allowed_bots: "yorkie-agent[bot],yorkie-agent"` (agent-iterate-ci.yml:328 and agent-review-panel.yml:1640) adds a second entry without the `[bot]` suffix. The repo's own trust argument for bot logins depends on that suffix being unregisterable — agent-iterate-ci.yml:182-184 ("GitHub reserves the `[bot]` suffix for Apps") and agent-review-panel.yml:210-221 for PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS. `yorkie-agent` without the suffix is an ordinary account/org name in the public namespace, so if claude-code-action compares the raw actor login rather than normalising away a `[bot]` suffix, the bare entry allow-lists any actor whose login is exactly `yorkie-agent`, not just this App. It is not exploitable today: to be the actor of these `workflow_run` events an account must have caused a CI run on a base-repo branch, and the fork check at agent-iterate-ci.yml:44 / agent-review-panel.yml:155 rejects fork-PR actors — hence minor rather than higher. Either drop the bare entry (if the action normalises, it is redundant) or state in the comment which matching rule of the pinned action makes it safe.
searchedFor: read both claude-code-action steps in full
checked gate `if:` fork/enable clauses in both workflows
checked PAGE_AUTHOR_LOGINS reserved-suffix rationale in both files

samples.summary: Branch-controlled CI failure text is emitted verbatim inside a fixed `HARNESS_EOF` heredoc into GITHUB_OUTPUT and then into the fixer prompt
samples.evidence: agent-iterate-ci.yml:287-292 captures `summarize-ci.mjs` stdout with a hard-coded delimiter (`echo "summary<<HARNESS_EOF"` … `echo "HARNESS_EOF"`). That stdout embeds `failureSummary` verbatim — scripts/agent/summarize-ci.mjs:97 does `out.push(`  ${failureSummary}`)`, and the two-space prefix applies only to the FIRST line, so any subsequent line of a multi-line build/test failure message is written unindented. A failure message whose body contains a line `HARNESS_EOF` therefore closes the heredoc early and the remaining bytes are parsed as further GITHUB_OUTPUT entries (arbitrary `key=value` for this step, or a malformed-file step failure). The same unsanitised text is interpolated into the fixer's prompt at line 336, so it can also forge the `</harness-diagnosis>` framing the surrounding "this is DATA, not instructions" guard relies on — against an agent holding Bash and the unscoped App token above. summarize-ci.mjs performs no delimiter filtering, escaping or truncation (whole file read; no `replace`/`slice` on the value). The archived adjudication that marked HARNESS_EOF a non-issue is explicitly scoped to the agent-implement kickoff prompt, whose content "is no longer agent-influenced" — docs/tasks/archive/2026/07/20260720-autonomous-issue-to-pr-pipeline-todo.md:172-174 — and does not cover this branch-derived path. Requires branch write access to reach, hence minor.

verdict.reason: Verified directly. agent-iterate-ci.yml:55-60 mints the App installation token with only app-id/private-key and NO permission-* scoping inputs; I read the entire 177-line file and this is its only create-github-app-token step. That token is persisted into the workspace .git/config (checkout at 62-66 passes token: and does not set persist-credentials: false; repo-wide grep finds persist-credentials only in agent-review-panel.yml:49,100,172 and agent-sdk-smoke-test.yml:33) and is passed as github_token: to claude-code-action at line 154, in a job that installs/executes checked-out branch code (line 125) and grants the agent Bash/Edit/Write (line 176) with branch-derived summarize-ci output interpolated into the prompt (line 165). The job-level permissions block (23-27) bounds GITHUB_TOKEN only, not the App token. Counterexample search came up empty: repo-wide grep for permission-contents / permission-pull-requests / permission-issues matches ONLY agent-review-panel.yml:379-381, whose comment states the exact rationale ("instead of inheriting the App installation's full permission set - this token is used in a job that checks out and executes untrusted branch code"), confirming the repo's own threat model for this pattern and its absence here. Note the finding's line numbers are wrong (real ones are 55-60 / 154 / 160, not 93-96 / 322 / 328) and its cited agent-fix.yml and agent-review-on-demand.yml do not exist in this repo, but the substantive defect is real at the actual locations. In lane (least-privilege / credential exposure) and blocking at major severity: an unbounded-scope credential reachable by a prompt-injectable agent with shell access; it is a weakness rather than a demonstrated exploit only because the installation's granted permission set is not readable from the repo.

verdict.reason: Core claim verified, though the reviewer's line numbers and corroborating citations are wrong. VERIFIED TRUE: agent-iterate-ci.yml:57 uses actions/create-github-app-token@v1, a mutable/retaggable ref, and line 60 passes private-key from secrets.AGENT_APP_PRIVATE_KEY into it, so the App private key itself (not a scoped installation token) is in that action's input scope. The neighbouring step in the SAME job at line 151 is SHA-pinned to anthropics/claude-code-action@af0559ee with the in-repo comment at line 149 'Pinned to the v1 release commit (immutable) for supply-chain safety' - the repo states the standard inline yet does not apply it to the step handling the more sensitive credential. Vector: whoever controls the v1 tag gets code execution in a job where the App private key is an input and can exfiltrate it; that key mints installation tokens for the whole installation indefinitely, strictly worse than a leaked short-lived token. VERIFIED FALSE but not rescuing a refutation: claimed lines 93/96/319 are really 57/60/151; the claimed comment 'this action handles the App private key' has zero matches in .github; and agent-fix.yml, agent-rerun.yml, agent-loop.yml, agent-summarize.yml and agent-review-on-demand.yml do not exist (only 9 workflow files). No create-github-app-token site is SHA-pinned - all four (agent-implement.yml:74, agent-iterate-ci.yml:57, agent-review-reply.yml:85, agent-review-panel.yml:371) use @v1, so the 'repo standard is the opposite' argument is wrong as stated, but that understates rather than overstates exposure. No refutation ground applies: code is present, no guard makes it unreachable, and supply-chain exposure of a credential is squarely in the secrets / sensitive-data-exposure lane. Inaccurate supporting citations are not a refutation ground when the primary evidence checks out.
